title: Remove @Beta from Multimaps.toMultimap()
body:
In some places of our project we are using toMultimap() method which is marked as @Beta and consequently is considered as an unstable API.

See:
https://github.com/google/guava/blob/d7a26416109381a6770681bc6c299567615e8341/guava/src/com/google/common/collect/Multimaps.java#L108

So. There is already 29.0 version of Google Guava. When does it gonna be considered as a "stable API"?
I would provide you more examples of  similar "unstable API" methods from Guava...

comments.body: Thanks for the request. Please note, as described [here](https://github.com/google/guava/wiki/PhilosophyExplained#beta-apis), Guava's beta APIs are well-tested. If your project is an application and not a library that is meant to be included in a different application, it's safe to use them.

@netdpb Yes, we use it in proprietary production grade product.
Hope to see it debetted in the next releases.
@netdpb I can even remove this annotation by myself and create a pull request.
Thanks, but because of our internal processes that actually makes it slightly more work for us. :D
@netdpb OK, won't create in this case :D
We're having an internal discussion about how to remove `@Beta` from lots more APIs, including this one. But we'll fast-forward this decision and get it out sooner.
